newsitem.title: USA: NYSE June 16-20 program trading averages 25.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE June 16-20 program trading averages 25.1 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading for the week of June 16-20 amounted to 132.7 million shares a day or 25.1 percent of the exchange's average daily volume of 529.2 million shares.
In the previous week, program trading accounted for 14.3 percent of average daily volume, or 76.7 million shares a day.
The exchange said buy programs accounted for 14.1 percent, and sell programs accounted for the remaining 11.0 percent of the average daily volume of program trades.
In all markets, program trading averaged 186.4 million shares a day during the week, the NYSE said.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, Natwest, Susquehanna Brokerage Services and BNP Securities each executed all of their program activity for customers, as agent. Morgan Stanley and First Boston executed most of their program trading activity as principal, for their own accounts.

Program volume executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 61.3 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 37.4 percent of program volume.

Between June 16 and June 20, 32.9 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 0.7 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, the exchange said.
